samples.summary: Keyboard toggle reads RAW run styles while the toolbar's getRangeStyleSummary() layers named-style inline defaults — the two still disagree (e.g. built-in Heading 6 is italic)
samples.evidence: New `isStyleOnInSelection` reads `(inline.style as Record<string, unknown>)[key]` with no named-style layer (packages/docs/src/view/text-editor.ts:3021), and its docstring claims it "Mirrors the toolbar's `getRangeStyleSummary()` decision so keyboard and toolbar agree". But the out-of-diff toolbar source layers style defaults: packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts:2847 `const defaults = styleDefaultsForBlock(block);` then `{ ...defaults, ...inline.style }` (editor.ts:2855). `BUILTIN_STYLES['heading-6'].inline` contains `italic: true` (packages/docs/src/model/named-styles.ts:91), and any user-redefined style can add bold/italic/underline (see packages/docs/test/model/named-styles.test.ts:97 producing `{fontSize:28, bold:true}`). Result: with a selection inside a Heading 6, the toolbar Italic button reads pressed and one click removes italic, while Cmd+I computes inRange=false and writes `italic:true` — a visually no-op first press, i.e. the same class of bug #715 the change claims to close. Fix belongs on the new `visit()` in text-editor.ts (layer `resolveStyleInline(blockStyleId(block), this.doc.document.styles)` under the run style), or the docstring's parity claim must be dropped.

samples.summary: Toolbar decision source (getRangeStyleSummary) does not descend into table blocks for cross-block selections, while the new keyboard read and the actual write do — the two paths now decide differently
samples.evidence: The new `isStyleOnInSelection` deliberately walks every cell of a table caught in a cross-block range (`visitTable`, text-editor.ts:3108-3110), mirroring `Doc.applyInlineStyle` (packages/docs/src/model/document.ts:415-428). The toolbar's now-authoritative source does not: packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts:2902-2907 iterates `doc.getContextBlocks()[i]` and calls `visitInlinesInBlock(block.id, ...)` even for `type === 'table'` blocks, whose own `inlines` are empty, so table cell runs never contribute. A selection spanning paragraph → table → paragraph therefore makes the toolbar B/I/U button decide add-vs-remove from the non-table paragraphs only, while `applyInlineStyle` writes into every cell and the keyboard shortcut decides from the cells too. Fix belongs in editor.ts's summary walk (add a table descent) so the two agree.

samples.summary: Shared toggles now call getRangeStyleSummary() on every render, replacing an O(1) caret read with a full-range walk for every consumer
samples.evidence: `text-format-group.tsx:96` calls `editor?.getRangeStyleSummary()` unconditionally during render, and `mobile-toolbar.tsx:229` does the same for slides. The docs implementation (packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts:2818-2946) walks every inline of the whole selection (including a full table-cell rectangle at editor.ts:2871-2889) and JSON.stringify-tokenizes 10 keys per run; the previous `getSelectionStyle()` read a single caret block. The docs toolbar already memoized this behind `onCursorMove` (docs-formatting-toolbar.tsx:317-323); the shared group does not, so a select-all on a large document re-walks the whole range on each toolbar re-render.

verdict.reason: Verified independently. text-editor.ts:3021 reads `inline.style[key]` raw with no named-style layer, while the toolbar's out-of-diff getRangeStyleSummary layers defaults (editor.ts:2847, 2855 via styleDefaultsForBlock at editor.ts:986-987). BUILTIN_STYLES['heading-6'].inline includes `italic: true` (named-styles.ts:91) and inline defaults are NOT materialized into runs — only block spacing is (named-styles.ts:146-151; inline cascade applied at layout time, layout.ts:150) — so Heading 6 runs carry `italic: undefined` yet render italic. The divergent consumer is reachable: docs toolbar Italic toggles from the layered summary (docs-formatting-toolbar.tsx:398) and Heading 6 is a selectable style (text-style-options.ts:88, applied at docs-formatting-toolbar.tsx:715), while Cmd+I routes through toggleStyle -> isStyleOnInSelection (text-editor.ts:875-878, 2894-2897) and computes inRange=false, writing italic:true as a visual no-op first press. The docstring's parity claim (text-editor.ts:2997-3000) is therefore false, and the inconsistency is only visible by leaving the diff, which is squarely this lens's lane (behaviour inconsistent with another module's established contract / consumer).

finding.summary: Slides mobile toolbar's B/I/U toggles still decide from `getSelectionStyle()` — the exact #715 mechanism the diff fixes, left in place on a shared-editor surface
finding.evidence: `packages/frontend/src/app/slides/toolbar/mobile-toolbar.tsx:225-234` still does `textEditor.applyStyle({ bold: !textEditor.getSelectionStyle().bold })` (and italic/underline), with `pressed={!!sel.bold}` from the same caret read at :240-253. `SlidesTextBoxEditor` exposes `getRangeStyleSummary()` (packages/slides/src/view/editor/text-box-editor.ts:240, delegating to packages/docs/src/view/text-box-editor.ts:1017), so the same backward-selection stuck-toggle bug is reachable there. Worse, the very same component renders `TextFormatSheet` → `TextFormatGroup` (mobile-toolbar.tsx:260, :552), which after this change decides from the range — so two Bold buttons in one bar now disagree. The task doc declares this out of scope (docs/tasks/active/20260810-docs-range-aware-toggles-todo.md:60), but the fix is one-line and the sibling site is a consumer of the same interface.

verdict.reason: The finding asserts the slides mobile toolbar's B/I/U toggles still decide from `getSelectionStyle()`. They do not. `packages/frontend/src/app/slides/toolbar/mobile-toolbar.tsx:229` reads `textEditor.getRangeStyleSummary()`, the click handlers at :232, :237, :242 invert `isStyleOn(textEditor.getRangeStyleSummary().<key>)`, and the pressed state at :252, :260, :268 uses `isStyleOn(summary.<key>)` — the exact range-aware form the diff establishes. `isStyleOn` is imported at :68 from the shared `packages/frontend/src/components/text-formatting/style-summary.ts:19`, the same predicate used by the shared `TextFormatGroup` rendered from this component via `TextFormatSheet` (:275 -> :567), so the claimed "two Bold buttons in one bar now disagree" does not occur. A repo-wide grep finds no `getSelectionStyle()` consumer in any frontend toolbar; the surviving references are only the `SlidesTextBoxEditor` interface/delegate (packages/slides/src/view/editor/text-box-editor.ts:239, 598-599), test fakes, and design docs. The quoted evidence (`applyStyle({ bold: !textEditor.getSelectionStyle().bold })` at :225-234 and `pressed={!!sel.bold}` at :240-253) does not exist in the file.

finding.summary: Cmd/Ctrl+B/I/U/S keyboard path still inverts the caret style, so the keyboard now disagrees with the toolbar it used to match
finding.evidence: `TextEditor.toggleStyle` (packages/docs/src/view/text-editor.ts:2875-2895) resolves `const base = this.getStyleAtCursor()` and does `resolved[key] = !visual[key]` for the shortcuts wired at :872-902. With a backward selection the caret sits at the range start and resolves the preceding run — the identical #715 defect. After this change the toolbar button renders unpressed (range says not-bold) while Ctrl+B removes bold, i.e. two entry points to the same mutation now behave differently. Acknowledged as a known limitation in docs/tasks/active/20260810-docs-range-aware-toggles-todo.md:52-56, but it is a reachable user path with no guard directing it through the new range-aware decision.

verdict.reason: The claimed bypass is not in the code. `toggleStyle` does not do `resolved[key] = !visual[key]`; at text-editor.ts:2889-2901 it computes `const inRange = this.isStyleOnInSelection(key)` and uses `!(inRange ?? !!visual[key])`, so the caret style is only a fallback when there is no selection (isStyleOnInSelection returns undefined only at :3007 for `!hasSelection() || !range`). The range walk explicitly normalizes selection direction — `visit(blockId, Math.min(a,b), Math.max(a,b))` at :3056-3059, and the analogous anchor/focus ordering at :3079-3081 and :3099-3103 — so a backward selection resolves the selected runs, not the preceding run, and mixed ranges set allOn=false (:3021) matching the toolbar's rule. All four shortcuts (:869-892) route through this same `toggleStyle`, and there is no other caret-only entry point for them (the remaining `getStyleAtCursor()` uses at :866 format-painter and :5306-5310 link-exit are unrelated). The cited "acknowledged limitation" is also misread: docs/tasks/active/20260810-docs-range-aware-toggles-todo.md:49-54 is a completed `- [x]` task describing this very fix, not a deferred limitation.
